title: Hosted API chat runbook + param lab demo
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording id: ff-20260302-7b2f
Files shared: deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/hosted-runbook), perf sheet (Google Drive link), security packet (link)

Summary: Short walkthrough of Hosted API chat basics focused on streaming behavior, param tuning, and retry patterns; live lab of a small prompt set; Q&A on security/compliance and next-step PoC options.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a short intro and then Diego will run the lab — quick note: the deck link is in the chat, and we'll drop the security pack at the end
[00:18] Lena (Aster): thanks, Maya; we're mostly focused on chat generation for triage workflows, low latency is important but cost matters too
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): yep, understood; latency vs cost is the classic tradeoff — i'll show streaming, batching, and then the retry patterns we recommend
[01:02] Marcus (Aster): we have a 300ms P95 target for short prompts, and a lot of concurrent users — also curious about private deployment for PHI
[01:20] Maya: perfect, we'll touch on hosted vs dedicated vs private during the q&a; Diego, take it away

[02:45] Diego: ok starting the console — this is the Redwood Console, the route is /v1/chat, sample SDK in the right panel. I'm going to send a short prompt to demo stream chunks
[03:10] Diego: (typing) sending prompt now — you'll notice the stream emits partial tokens, and the client can render as they arrive. If there is a transient backend issue we recommend an idempotent request id and client-side retry with exponential backoff
[04:05] Priya: quick question, do you guarantee chunk order? We had weird reordering in another service
[04:18] Diego: good Q, we keep chunk ordering per-request — reorders only happen if you stitch responses from different model variants, but per connection ordering is stable
[05:30] Lena: what's the recommended retry window? like how long to wait before falling back to a faster smaller model
[05:45] Diego: typical pattern — try two fast retries at 300-500ms backoff, then fallback to a cheaper variant, e.g., 8-bit quantized model. In the Console you can set automatic fallback policies per-route
[06:12] Maya: we also have a feature in Optimize that will suggest batching and quantization settings based on your prompt mix — it generated the suggestion in our perf sheet for your sample data

[07:40] Diego: live lab: Marcus you gave us three representative prompts; i'll run them repeated to mimic concurrent users. Note: i'm enabling KV cache prefixing for repeated prompts — we sometimes see the transcription show K V cash which is funny in the notes
[08:10] (sound of keyboard)
[09:00] Diego: first run — P50 is ~120ms, P95 ~360ms for single token streaming on a c-snapshot; note these are hosted numbers and will change with sequence length
[10:10] Marcus: those numbers are pretty close to our target, how does batching affect tail latency?
[10:30] Diego: batching increases throughput but can increase tail. We recommend small max-batch sizes with latency SLOs turned on so the router will prefer latency nodes for those routes
[11:05] Priya: can you explain the router preference thing quickly?
[11:15] Diego: sure — Smart routing can send low-latency traffic to fast pool (dedicated) and less-sensitive traffic to cheaper pools; you can set per-route policy in the Console. If fast pool is saturated it will automatically fallback to compatible model variants so requests don't fail

[12:40] Lena: security — we need SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. How mature is the private deployment?
[12:55] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML and OIDC, and audit logs with token-level traces in the Console. For private we do a VPC control plane option and on-prem packages that integrate with customer KMS or an HSM
[13:30] Lena: good, and data residency? we need EU data stay in eu
[13:36] Diego: routing by region is supported, and you can restrict model serving to region-specific pools — we'll include the compliance notes in the packet we share

[15:05] Diego: switching back to demo — i'm going to trigger an artificial throttle to show client-side retries and server side 429 handling
[15:33] (beep)
[15:46] Diego: you can see the client retry with an idempotency token and then stream resumes from the last emitted partial chunk; if you want guaranteed no-duplicate tokens we recommend explicit dedupe on the client when reconstituting stream fragments
[16:40] Marcus: interesting — how do you handle token-level costs with retries? we worry about double-charging
[16:55] Maya: cost attribution is token-level and we surface retry-attributed tokens separately in the Console. Also Optimize can recommend caching thresholds to avoid retrying long sequences
[17:30] Priya: can we do a quick check on prompt truncation behavior? sometimes other APIs drop context
[17:45] Diego: we support clear signals: you can set truncate behavior to preserve last N tokens or raise an error. The SDK will return an explicit code when truncation occurs, so you can detect and handle it

[19:10] Diego: now a short explanation of parameters — temperature controls randomness, top_p for nucleus sampling, max_tokens for response length. For chat we also have system message weighting and regeneration parameters in the Console
[19:45] Priya: do you recommend deterministic settings for triage?
[19:50] Diego: yes, lower temperature (0.0-0.2) and top_p 0.8-1.0 to keep things stable, plus a short max_tokens cap since triage answers are brief

[21:02] Maya: Pete from our security team asked earlier about audit exports — we can deliver log exports to your S3 or your on-prem SIEM
[21:20] Lena: perfect, that helps the compliance team. Do you have a runbook for incident response?
[21:30] Maya: yes, we'll share a runbook — it's a living doc that covers fallback policies and observability hooks

[23:10] Diego: running a longer workload now to show resource behavior — note, the runtime will pick kernels based on sequence length and model architecture; in our notes we sometimes see kernel names like gemm32 (transcribed as gem 32) so forgive the spellings in the transcript
[24:18] (typing and console output)
[25:02] Diego: long-run numbers: with automatic batching and prefix caching we saw 2.3x cost reduction on this prompt mix in our lab compared to naive per-request serving. The perf sheet link has details
[26:00] Marcus: sounds good — what's the onboarding friction? can we do a PoC in two weeks?
[26:12] Maya: yes, typical PoC is 2-4 weeks; we can do a minimal pilot on hosted, then if you need VPC or dedicated we help with sizing and pilot plan
[27:05] Priya: and pricing for PoC?
[27:12] Maya: we'll send a pilot pricing estimate — usually it's usage plus a small integration credit; Diego will attach a sample PoC template

[28:40] Diego: technical note — for clients with very tight deterministic budgets we recommend quantized variants and the Optimize suggestions; for very low-latency interactive flows we recommend smaller max-batch and reserved capacity (Dedicated)
[29:55] Marcus: do you expose tokenizers in the SDK or is it opaque?
[30:05] Diego: the SDK includes tokenization utilities and conservative token count estimates in the Console so you can estimate cost. For exact accounting we show tokenization on the request trace

[32:20] Lena: competitor question — we've tried some self-host and also evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; how do you differentiate on operations?
[32:35] Maya: Redwood focuses on the entire serving stack: predictable latency, observability at token-level, and integrated cost-optimizations in Optimize; we provide the runtime + orchestration which reduces ops work vs building yourself
[33:10] Priya: any gotchas with SAML and provisioning?
[33:20] Maya: standard SAML flows, SCIM provisioning supported; we'll send our integration notes

[34:40] Diego: demo: i'm going to simulate a model variant fallback. watch console: when the fast pool is saturated it will reroute to a quantized variant with minimal param changes — streaming resumes and client sees a short gap but no error
[35:05] (brief audio)
[36:10] Marcus: for our PHI flows, is there an option to keep logs from leaving our VPC?
[36:25] Maya: yes with Private deployment logs can be kept on-prem or routed to your S3; hosted has strict retention but for PHI we recommend private or dedicated with controlled exports

[37:40] Priya: ok, last quick one — threading and conversation history, do you store convo state in Redwood or do you recommend external state store?
[37:55] Diego: we support session KV cache for short-term history and persistent storage is optional; many customers store canonical history externally and use KV cache for recent tokens

[39:10] Maya: we're nearly out of time; quick recap of actions and next steps
[39:25] Lena: thanks, this was really helpful — i'm going to loop in compliance and infra and we'll pick which pilot flavor we want
[39:40] Maya: great — Diego, can you run that 1k concurrency perf and share results?
[39:48] Diego: yep, i'll run it and post results in the perf sheet by Friday
[40:00] (crosstalk)
[40:15] Marcus: will you share the PO C template?
[40:22] Maya: yes, sending after the call
[40:45] Priya: one more — can we have a technical deep dive next week if we choose private?
[40:55] Maya: absolutely, we'll coordinate times — Diego and our infra engineer can join

[42:10] Diego: final note on instrumentation: you can set token-level alerts in Console, and Optimize ties regressions to specific prompt sets so you can roll back model versions quickly
[42:40] Maya: thanks again everyone, we'll drop the links and action items into the calendar invite
[43:05] Lena: bye all
[43:10] (meeting end)
summary: AE/SE walkthrough of Hosted API chat basics with a live parameter lab. Demonstrated streaming chunks, retry/backoff patterns, fallback to quantized variants, batching tradeoffs, and Console/Optimize features. Discussed compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS), private deployment options for PHI, and agreed on a PoC. SE to run perf tests and Redwood to send security docs and PO C template.
